chunks: Among his proofs (peace be upon him) is that he said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, did not make for people a proof in their deeds except through an Imam who guides them or a Messenger who warns them.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine proof for human deeds according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this foundational hadith to articulate the Shia doctrine of *Hujjah* (divine proof), emphasizing that Allah’s justice necessitates an infallible guide (*Imam*) or a warning Messenger (*Nabi*) to make religious obligations clear to humanity. This establishes the Imamate not merely as a political institution but as an epistemological necessity for interpreting divine law and ensuring the continuity of guidance after the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).
